shortDefinition: Controls and constraints that prevent an AI model from generating harmful or inappropriate outputs.
fullDefinition: Guardrails are the safety mechanisms built into AI systems to prevent harmful outputs — including content filters, topic restrictions, format validation, and safety classifiers. They operate at multiple levels: model training (RLHF), inference time (content filters), and application layer (custom rules). Guardrails reduce risk but can also over-refuse legitimate requests.
examples: ChatGPT refusing to provide instructions for dangerous activities
A customer service AI refusing to discuss competitors
